thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging #eng-oncall: p99 latency spike detected for continuous-batching path (us-west2). p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 2.3s over the last 5m. Streaming stalls increased to 12%. Auto-alert opened: INC-276544.
maya (oncall): saw it, on it. grabbing metrics + logs now. @alex can you take runtime triage?
alex (eng-runtime): looking. quick summary from histogram: steady state p99 ~380ms. spike started at ~2765439900. Sampling traces show long tail inside batcher scheduling and KV cache access. Many batches assembled with mixed seq lengths, batch sizes jumping to 48-64; scheduler fairness seems to prioritize oldest reqs which are long, blocking smaller streaming requests.
sam (sre): any increased eviction or OOMs? node CPU/GPU looks fine, no OOMs. but we see queue depth for cont-batch up x3.
zara (eng-platform): config snapshot shows schedule_weights = [age:0.8, size:0.2] — that could explain age bias. we deployed that weight change in last config rollout ~12h ago.
nora (prod-support): ticket flood? we've seen 6 customer errors in the last 10m, three are streaming timeouts, two are retries flagged as 429 from client SDK. CS notified.
jeff (cs): two customers on Dedicated impacted (account ids redacted). reaching out: low severity but they noticed higher latency on streaming endpoints.
maya (oncall): OK proposed mitigations:
1) short term (live mitigation, <10m): reduce max_batch_size for cont-batch to 32 and enable preempt_small_streaming=true so streaming reqs can preempt long batched work. apply as canary to one shard in us-west2.
2) mid term (30-120m): enable seq-length bucketing for top-10 models to avoid mixing 4-token and 1200-token requests in same batch.
3) post-mitigation: revert scheduler_weights to age:0.5,size:0.5 and monitor.
alex (eng-runtime): I can push the short-term change. will flip max_batch_size at runtime via ops API on canary shard.

---
Command I'll run (canary):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API" \ 
  https://ops-api.redwood.internal/v1/configs/cont-batch/us-west2/canary \ 
  -d '{"scheduler.max_batch_size":32, "scheduler.enable_preempt_small_streaming":true}'
```

Sample batcher log around spike:
```
[batcher] assembled_batch id=0x7f size=58 seq_mix=[4, 3, 1200, 50, 8, ...] latency_wait=1187ms
[batcher] schedule_attempt blocked_by=long_seq age_head=3.4s
[kv] cache_hit=false key=abc123 lookup_ms=1120
```
---
sam (sre): note: preempt flag will cause partial batches to be executed more often — increases token cost slightly but reduces tail latency. agree canary.
zara (eng-platform): I will route 5% traffic to canary shard and add additional alert for p99>700ms.

maya (oncall): alex please run the curl and paste response. monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall %. sam help watch infra metrics.
alex (eng-runtime): running now... paste response: `{"status":"applied","target":"us-west2-canary","changes":["scheduler.max_batch_size=32","scheduler.enable_preempt_small_streaming=true"]}`. canary ingress switched.

maya (oncall): initial observations: canary p99 down from 2.3s -> 560ms in 3m. streaming stalls down to 3%. routing 5% was enough to see effect.

nora (prod-support): customer update: sent note to 3 impacted customers saying we're mitigating and will follow up within hour. :thumbsup:
jeff (cs): ack, I'll keep customers in loop.

alex (eng-runtime): mid-term change: enabling seq-length bucketing requires model group config change. sample config snippet:
```
models:
  - name: text-stream-v2
    batching:
      seq_buckets: [0-32, 33-256, 257-2048]
      max_batch_per_bucket: [64, 48, 8]
```
I can stage that to canary after we confirm canary stability.
sam (sre): monitoring: adding temporary alert for queue_depth > 200 and kv_miss_rate > 5%.

maya (oncall): escalation? any need to page exec or infra? looks like mitigations effective. no customers requesting immediate SLA credits.

ops-bot: INC-276544 updated: status -> mitigated on canary. linked runbook: https://runbook.internal/cont-batch-tail

maya (oncall): ok I'll do a short handoff to night oncall. notes to pass along:
- root cause: config drift towards age-heavy scheduling + mixed seq-length workload causing large mixed batches and KV lookups blocking streaming.
- mitigation applied: canary reduced max_batch_size=32 and enabled preempt_small_streaming. immediate p99 improvement observed.
- next steps for oncall: 1) after 30m, if p99 stable <700ms, roll change to remaining shards (gradually). 2) stage seq-length bucketing for top models and monitor cost impact. 3) follow up with platform to revert scheduler_weights to balanced and add automated seq-bucketing rule for models with heavy seq variance.
- customer comms: prod-support sent targeted messages; CS tracking two Dedicated customers.

maya (oncall): handing over to @zara for rollout and @sam for monitoring. I'm off in 10m. :raised_hand:
zara (eng-platform): roger. will continue rollout to remaining us-west2 shards at 10% increments, watching p99 and token cost.
sam (sre): will keep the alert page open for 2h window.
jeff (cs): I'll follow up with customers and flag any further escalations.

maya (oncall): thanks team. leaving thread. last note: INC-276544 -> mitigated->monitoring. will file postmortem if rollout shows reoccurrence. :eyes:
ops-bot: INC-276544 status changed to monitoring by maya
zara (eng-platform): (10m after) rolled to 30% - p99 stable 480ms. continuing.
sam (sre): (30m after) kv_miss_rate normalized to baseline. no further pages.
maya (oncall): (handoff) signing off. next_oncall: @nora (night).
